key_insight: Coherent noise drives the triangular-lattice surface code into a partially decodable critical phase, dual to algebraic strong-to-weak symmetry breaking in a quantum paramagnet.
engineering_relevance: The results show that coherent errors can produce recovery regimes beyond a simple decodable-versus-undecodable picture, motivating noise-aware evaluation of surface-code decoders.
method: Study single-qubit Pauli-Z rotations followed by syndrome measurements in the surface code.
Relate decoding to strongly symmetric decoherence in a dual Z₂ paramagnet.
Derive universal observables using an SO(n) nonlinear sigma model in the replica limit n→1.
evidence_signal: Large-scale numerical simulations confirm analytical predictions for aspect-ratio-dependent optimal Pauli decoding fidelity and power-law decay of the dual fidelity correlator.
watch_item: The predictions concern a specific coherent-noise model and optimal Pauli decoding; practical decoder performance under realistic mixed noise remains to be established.
paper_title: Algebraic strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and partial decodability in the surface code
